promise: Ctrl-C during `hangar --exec` leaves nothing running, at one host at a time and in parallel, and the run says it was interrupted.
why: Shipped in 0027 as a documented caveat: Foundation starts each command in its own process group, so the terminal's SIGINT reached hangar and not them, and the commands kept running reparented to init with no deadline over them. Drives the built binary on a real pty through scripts/exec-terminal-check.sh, with SIGINT reset first, because a job from a non-interactive shell starts with it ignored and the first version of this check passed for that reason alone. The pty stays open while it looks, because closing it hangs up the session and kills the orphans a real terminal keeps. Watched failing on the commit before 0036. interrupt-after-a-death covers a command at --parallel 2 that killed itself with SIGINT: that once marked the run interrupted, and Ctrl-C then did nothing until the other command finished. Its first version matched `alpha*` against aliases that start with the product, so no command ever died and it passed at 6b53d57 as well; with the pattern fixed it was watched failing there. interrupt-background covers a job a command started with `&` at one host at a time: a shell starts it ignoring SIGINT, so it outlived the leader Ctrl-C killed. Watched failing at 7dcd99f.
command: scripts/exec-terminal-check.sh interrupt && scripts/exec-terminal-check.sh interrupt-parallel && scripts/exec-terminal-check.sh interrupt-after-a-death && scripts/exec-terminal-check.sh interrupt-background
